pr.title: More ptr metadata gvn
pr.description:
There's basically 3 parts to this PR.

1. Allow references as arguments to `UnOp::PtrMetadata` 
 
This is a MIR semantics addition, so
r? mir

Rather than just raw pointers, also allow references to be passed to `PtrMetadata`.  That means the length of a slice can be just `PtrMetadata(_1)` instead of also needing a ref-to-pointer statement (`_2 = &raw *_1` + `PtrMetadata(_2)`).

AFAIK there should be no provenance or tagging implications of looking at the *metadata* of a pointer, and the code in the backends actually already supported it (other than a debug assert, given that they don't care about ptr vs reference, really), so we might as well allow it.

2. Simplify the argument to `PtrMetadata` in GVN

Because the specific kind of pointer-like thing isn't that important, GVN can simplify all those details away.  Things like `*const`-to-`*mut` casts and `&mut`-to-`&` reborrows are irrelevant, and skipping them lets it see more interesting things.

cc @cjgillot 

Notably, unsizing casts for arrays.  GVN supported that for `Len`, and now it sees it for `PtrMetadata` as well, allowing `PtrMetadata(pointer)` to become a constant if that pointer came from an array-to-slice unsizing, even through a bunch of other possible steps.

3. Replace `NormalizeArrayLen` with GVN

The `NormalizeArrayLen` pass hasn't been running even in optimized builds for well over a year, and it turns out that GVN -- which *is* on in optimized builds -- can do everything it was trying to do.

So the code for the pass is deleted, but the tests are kept, just changed to the different pass.

As part of this, `LowerSliceLen` was changed to emit `PtrMetadata(_1)` instead of `Len(*_1)`, a small step on the road to eventually eliminating `Rvalue::Len`.

analysis.incorrectTransformation: Incorrect foil (warned against by the source, not the merged implementation): while simplifying a `UnOp::PtrMetadata` operand, unconditionally erase every `CastKind::PtrToPtr` and every address/deref reborrow without checking that the pointee metadata is preserved, and fold any pointer cast into a constant length. That would rewrite `PtrMetadata` across metadata-removing casts such as `*const [T] -> *const T` or across different generic tails such as `*const A -> *const B`, silently changing the metadata value. The source explicitly warns: "It's critical that this not eliminate cases like `*const [T]` -> `*const T` which remove metadata." A second foil is folding a `PtrMetadata` of a non-`PointerCoercion(Unsize)` cast to an array length; only an unsizing array-to-slice cast assigns length to fat-pointer metadata.
analysis.inputDomain: Runtime-phase MIR containing `Rvalue::UnaryOp(UnOp::PtrMetadata, arg)` where `arg` is an `&`/`&mut`/`*const`/`*mut` operand whose definition chain includes: (a) `Rvalue::Cast(CastKind::PtrToPtr, ...)` pointer casts (including `*const`<->`*mut` and generic pointee changes), (b) `Rvalue::Ref`/`Rvalue::AddressOf` of a place of the exact form `Deref` of a tracked local, or (c) `Rvalue::Cast(CastKind::PointerCoercion(PointerCoercion::Unsize), ...)` from `&[T; N]`/`*[T; N]`-like array pointee to slice pointee. The function may be generic over unsized pointees, so metadata types can be unknown.
analysis.originalLogic: Pre-PR GVN `simplify_unary(&mut self, op: UnOp, value: VnIndex)` matched only value-numbered operands and handled `PtrMetadata` only for a visible `Value::Aggregate(AggregateType::RawPtr, _, fields)` by returning `fields[1]`; it did not normalize the argument through pointer casts or reborrows, nor fold array-unsize metadata. Separately, `NormalizeArrayLen` performed an SSA-based analysis mapping slice locals to array-length constants, and `LowerSliceLenCalls` emitted `Rvalue::Len(tcx.mk_place_deref(arg))`. The PR description states: "The `NormalizeArrayLen` pass hasn't been running even in optimized builds for well over a year, and it turns out that GVN -- which *is* on in optimized builds -- can do everything it was trying to do."
pitfalls: Do not eliminate a `PtrToPtr` cast when metadata differs; `*const [T] -> *const T` changes metadata from `usize` to `()` and must remain.

Do not compare only tail types when metadata types are known and differ: the equality is on the `ptr_metadata_ty_or_tail` result, so `Ok(meta_ty)` equality and `Err(tail_ty)` equality are distinct; a known/unknown mismatch is not equal.
Do not fold `PtrMetadata` for casts other than an array-to-slice unsizing cast; only that cast stores the array length in the fat pointer.
Do not strip an `Address`/reborrow whose place projection is not exactly a single `Deref`; other projections may change the referent.
GVN runs on potentially generic MIR, so exact metadata types may be unnormalized; the identity closure passed to `ptr_metadata_ty_or_tail` is deliberate.

Removing `NormalizeArrayLen` from the pipeline and retargeting its tests to GVN does not mean the old pass output was correct or that retained test names prove the replacement; compare actual value assignments.
Validator must accept `ty::Ref(..)` as well as `ty::RawPtr(..)` for PtrMetadata, and must still reject it outside Runtime MIR.
`LowerSliceLenCalls` should not construct `Len(*_1)` anymore; the new form is `PtrMetadata(_1)` with the original operand.
preconditions: PtrMetadata is allowed in Runtime MIR only and, after this PR, accepts both unsafe pointers and references: validator checks `ty::RawPtr(..) | ty::Ref(..)`.

A `PtrToPtr` cast may be skipped only when `from.builtin_deref(true).unwrap().ptr_metadata_ty_or_tail(tcx, |t| t)` equals the same computation for `to`; this compares known metadata types or, when metadata is unknown, the tail type.
An `Address`/reborrow value may be skipped only when its place is exactly `PlaceRef { local, projection: [PlaceElem::Deref] }` and that local has a value number.
Folding to a constant requires `CastKind::PointerCoercion(PointerCoercion::Unsize)` with `to`'s pointee being a slice and `from`'s pointee being an array with known length.
If the operand changes during simplification, the new operand must be materialized via `try_as_operand`: a constant if value-numbered as constant, otherwise a copy of a reusable local.
`LowerSliceLenCalls` now recognizes `func.const_fn_def()` and emits `Rvalue::UnaryOp(UnOp::PtrMetadata, arg.node.clone())` so the operand itself is the reference rather than a deref place.
analysis.summary: GVN was taught to normalize the operand of `UnOp::PtrMetadata`: strip metadata-preserving `PtrToPtr` casts and address/deref reborrows, then fold `PtrMetadata` of an array-to-slice unsizing cast to the array length constant. The PR also widens PtrMetadata MIR semantics to references, replaces the non-running `NormalizeArrayLen` pass with GVN, and makes `LowerSliceLenCalls` emit `PtrMetadata(_1)` instead of `Len(*_1)`. Reusable knowledge is the metadata-equivalence invariant that every cast elimination must satisfy.
analysis.testStrategy: Use `tests/mir-opt/gvn.rs` with `//@ test-mir-pass: GVN` and `#![feature(custom_mir)]`. Add (1) `manual_slice_mut_len(&mut [i32])`: reborrow to `*mut [i32]`, `PtrToPtr` to `*const [i32]`, then `ptr_metadata`; expect `_0 = PtrMetadata(_1)`. (2) `array_len(&mut [i32; 42])`: unsize array to slice then `ptr_metadata`; expect `_0 = const 42_usize`. (3) `generic_cast_metadata<T, A: ?Sized, B: ?Sized>` using `CastPtrToPtr` and `PtrMetadata` with paired CHECK lines: metadata `usize -> ()` (`*const [T]` to `*const T`) must not optimize; `(&A, [T])` vs `[T]` has matching `usize` metadata and must optimize to `PtrMetadata(_1)`; tail `A` vs tail `B` must not optimize; matching tail `A` must optimize to `PtrMetadata(_2)`; `*const B`/`*mut A` mismatched tails must not optimize; `*const B`/`*mut B` matching tails must optimize to `PtrMetadata(_3)`. Also retarget `tests/mir-opt/lower_array_len.rs` to `//@ test-mir-pass: GVN` and keep array/bound/reborrow/raw/by-value cases expecting `const N`; check `lower_slice_len.bound...` now expects `_5 = PtrMetadata(move _6)`; check pre-codegen slice indexing/iteration MIR uses `PtrMetadata(_1)`. Do not claim execution; these are MIR-dump expectations only.
analysis.trigger: GVN encounters a `PtrMetadata` unary operation whose operand value number is a pointer-preserving cast, a bare reborrow/address-of of a dereferenced local, or an array-to-slice unsizing cast; it then walks backward through metadata-preserving casts/reborrows and may replace the whole operation with a constant or with `PtrMetadata` of an earlier pointer/reference.
